R1_connectivity.summary: Audit of connectivity metrics (component fractions, torus winding, susceptibility) and finite-size boundary evidence across L=12, 18, 24 reveals three implementation/metric artifacts and two severe finite-size/sampling limitations. Specifically: (1) torus winding booleans test coordinate differences along non-orthogonal steps rather than cycle-space rank, allowing a single 1D diagonal cycle in direction (-1,1) to set both wrap_basis_1 and wrap_basis_2 to True; (2) susceptibility normalizes by residual nodes (N - s_max) while including isolated vertices (s=1), pinning fully condensed hub-biased states to susceptibility=1.0 and causing supercritical non-monotonicity from single dimers; (3) topological percolation/wrapping (complete by z=2.4 for arms 0-2) is decoupled from mechanical eligibility (0/4 eligible pairs at L=24, z=2.4); (4) hub-biased rewiring (arm 3) causes size-dependent fragmentation that worsens with L; and (5) n=4 correlated seeds on a coarse delta_z=0.4 grid with size-dependent edge rounding cannot resolve finite-size phase boundaries.

findings.title: Torus winding metric conflates single diagonal (-1,1) cycles with 2D biconnected wrapping
findings.evidence: Lattice steps are [(1,0), (0,1), (-1,1)] (line 12), and cycle closure sets wrap[k] |= diff[k] != 0 for k in (0,1) across all components (lines 49, 60).
findings.implication: A single 1D cycle wrapping only along the third lattice direction (-1,1) produces diff = (-L, +L), setting both wrap_basis_1 and wrap_basis_2 to True without two independent torus cycles or 2D spanning topology. Moreover, wrap is aggregated globally across all components rather than restricted to the largest component.
findings.recommended_check: Compute the integer winding vectors (w1, w2) = (diff[0]//L, diff[1]//L) per connected component and report both single-direction wrapping (rank >= 1) and 2D biconnected wrapping (matrix rank == 2 of cycle winding vectors within the largest component).

findings.title: Susceptibility normalization by (N - s_max) with s=1 isolates creates supercritical artifacts and masks hub fragmentation
findings.evidence: susceptibility is computed as sum(s*s for s in small)/max(1, sum(small)) where small = sizes[1:] includes isolated degree-0 vertices (s=1).
findings.implication: When all vertices outside the largest component are isolated nodes (s=1), susceptibility is identically 1.0 even when 11% to 68% of the network is disconnected (e.g., arm 3 at L=12 across z=1.2 to 4.8 in analysis/graph-summary.csv lines 5-29). Conversely, in supercritical uniform graphs (L=12, arm 0), susceptibility rises non-monotonically from 1.198 at z=2.4 to 1.417 at z=3.2 (analysis/graph-summary.csv lines 14, 18) because a single residual dimer (s=2) when N - s_max is tiny yields 4/2 = 2.0.
findings.recommended_check: Report standard volume-normalized susceptibility sum(s*s for s in small)/N alongside mean cluster size excluding isolated degree-0 vertices (s > 1).

findings.title: Complete eligibility collapse at L=24, z=2.4 separates connectivity percolation from mechanical rigidity
findings.evidence: At L=24, z_target=2.4, eligible_pairs is 0 out of 4 for all contrasts (hub_minus_uniform and triangle_high_minus_low) across kappa=0.0, 0.003, and 0.03 (lines 1451-1504), even though arms 0-2 have largest_component_mean > 0.909 and wrap_basis_1_mean = wrap_basis_2_mean = 1.0 (lines 1180-1227).
findings.implication: Connectivity spanning (z_c ~ 2.0) does not confer mechanical eligibility (G0 > 1e-6) at z=2.4, and hub-biased rewiring (arm 3) additionally destroys topological wrapping at L=24, z=2.4 (wrap_basis_1_mean = 0.0, largest_component_mean = 0.446). Consequently, no matched-stiffness mechanical contrast survives at z=2.4 for the largest system size.
findings.recommended_check: Report per-arm G0 distributions and eligibility counts across all (L, z, arm) settings and test sensitivity of matched contrasts to the G0 > 1e-6 operational threshold.

findings.title: Hub-biased rewiring (arm 3) exhibits non-convergent finite-size fragmentation as L increases
findings.evidence: In arm 3 at z_target=2.4, increasing L from 12 to 18 to 24 causes largest_component_mean to fall (0.535 -> 0.486 -> 0.446), wrap_basis_2_mean to drop (0.50 -> 0.25 -> 0.00), and susceptibility_mean to surge (1.015 -> 3.340 -> 10.007) (rows 17, 45, 73); a similar susceptibility jump (1.010 -> 1.600 -> 8.533) occurs at z_target=1.2 (rows 5, 33, 61).
findings.implication: Fixed-length 100*N hub-biased MCMC chains drive finite-size condensation into dense multi-hub clusters rather than a scale-invariant topology ensemble, shifting the apparent connectivity boundary to higher z as system size grows.
findings.recommended_check: Track component count, isolated-node fraction, and largest-component scaling versus MCMC proposal count and system size L to determine whether arm 3 approaches a single condensed cluster or multiple disconnected hubs at large L.

findings.title: Coarse z grid, n=4 correlated seeds, and edge-count rounding preclude finite-size boundary estimation
findings.evidence: Per-direction edge count round(z*N/6) causes z_actual to drift across L (at z_target=1.6: 1.583, 1.593, 1.604; at z_target=2.4: 2.417, 2.407, 2.396 in analysis/graph-summary.csv), while only 4 seeds per L are run on a coarse z grid (spacing 0.4) reusing identical seed streams across z (line 108).
findings.implication: At z=2.0 (arm 0), wrap_basis_1_mean fluctuates non-monotonically across sizes (0.25 at L=12, 0.75 at L=18, 0.50 at L=24; analysis/graph-summary.csv rows 10, 38, 66) because 0.25 corresponds to a single graph realization. Finite-size crossings for connectivity or rigidity transitions cannot be statistically localized.
findings.recommended_check: Use independent RNG seeds per (L, z) point (e.g., SeedSequence spawning), increase replication (>= 32 seeds), and evaluate finite-size scaling against exact realized z_actual on a finer grid (delta_z <= 0.05) around z in [1.8, 3.6].

R1_connectivity.strongest_surviving_claim: In the well-connected supercritical regime (z_target = 4.8, where arms 0, 1, and 2 achieve 100% component connectivity and torus wrapping across all sizes and arm 3 maintains >86% largest-component fraction with full wrapping), all 4 seed pairs at L=24 are mechanically eligible and show that under selective axial relaxation (r=0.5), hub-biased networks exhibit lower stress retention than uniform networks (retention delta = -0.0194 at kappa=0.003 and -0.0392 at kappa=0.03), although this contrast remains confounded by the co-change in clustering, degree variance, and ~13.4% disconnected nodes in arm 3.
R1_connectivity.decisive_next_experiment: Run a dedicated connectivity-and-rigidity finite-size sweep across L in {12, 18, 24, 36} with >= 32 independent RNG seeds per (L, z) on a fine coordination grid (z in [1.8, 3.6], step 0.1), recording exact homology winding rank (rank 1 vs rank 2 in the giant component), volume-normalized susceptibility sum(s^2)/N, and unfiltered G0 values to separate the connectivity percolation threshold from the central-force and bending rigidity thresholds.

R2_clustering.summary: Audit of the CPU clustering and hub-bias intervention campaign confirms that the graph generator strictly enforces total edge count, directional edge balance, and (for hexagon-flip arms 1 and 2) exact node degree sequences, while the linearized solver passes self-tests, translational invariance, and elastic retention nulls. However, substantive topological conclusions are limited by three primary threats to validity: (1) the alternating-hexagon MCMC proposal in arms 1 and 2 has very low acceptance and neutral-move mixing, achieving only a 0.0037 to 0.0230 clustering contrast in mechanically eligible regimes; (2) collinear bending motifs (bends) are unconstrained during graph interventions and omitted from graph summaries, confounding topological contrasts when kappa > 0 and driving sign reversals in G0_delta_mean across kappa; and (3) the hub-biased edge replacement (arm 3) strongly co-changes triangle clustering (by 1.5x to 25x) while fragmenting the largest connected component and breaking periodic wrapping.

findings.title: Minimal achieved clustering contrast in degree-preserving hexagon-flip interventions
findings.evidence: At L=24, z_target=4.8 (lines 82-84), triangle-biased (arm 1) and triangle-suppressed (arm 2) chains accept only 114.75 and 112.0 moves out of 57,600 proposals (~0.20%), shifting mean triangles from 589.0 to 593.5 (0.76%) and clustering from 0.3156 to 0.3192 (delta = 0.00366). Across all mechanically eligible regimes (z >= 3.2), the clustering contrast between arm 1 and arm 2 never exceeds 0.023.
findings.implication: Near-zero mechanical differences in triangle_high_minus_low reflect a tiny realized structural perturbation from sparse alternating-hexagon proposals and unit-probability neutral moves (source/cpu-sweep.py lines 33-36), rather than demonstrating that network viscoelasticity is insensitive to clustering at fixed degree sequence.
findings.recommended_check: Sample directly from indexed active alternating hexagons (rejection-free proposal) with stronger inverse temperature |beta| > 2 and longer chains to verify whether a larger degree-preserving clustering contrast (e.g., delta clustering >= 0.05) is achievable on the triangular lattice, or restrict claims to the realized 1%-6% triangle perturbation.

findings.title: Uncontrolled collinear bending-motif confounding across triangle and hub interventions
findings.evidence: Collinear bending energy (lines 74-81) acts on consecutive active edges in the same direction (nb, logged as bends at line 100), which are neither preserved by hexagon flips or hub swaps nor reported in analysis/graph-summary.csv. In analysis/paired-summary.csv, G0_delta_mean for triangle_high_minus_low at L=24, z=4.0 reverses sign from +0.00096 at kappa=0 (line 117) to -0.00429 at kappa=0.03 (line 121), and hub_minus_uniform at L=24, z=4.8 reverses from +0.03419 at kappa=0 (line 122) to -0.00950 at kappa=0.03 (line 126).
findings.implication: Condensing edges into triangles or hubs interrupts straight collinear fibers and alters active bending motif counts (nb), so increasing kappa differentially stiffens uniform and low-triangle networks and confounds mechanical contrasts at kappa > 0.
findings.recommended_check: Export bends (nb) into analysis/graph-summary.csv, report paired delta_bends for all contrasts, and either constrain MCMC moves to preserve collinear two-edge counts or control for delta_bends when interpreting G0 and retention shifts.

findings.title: Hub-biased intervention co-changes triangle clustering and fragments the percolating component
findings.evidence: At L=24, z_target=3.2 (lines 74, 77), hub-biased replacement (arm 3) increases triangles_mean from 176.5 (arm 0) to 544.5 and transitivity_mean from 0.2150 to 0.3916 (far exceeding arm 1's 181.25 triangles), while reducing largest_component_mean from 0.985 to 0.638 and wrap_basis_1_mean from 1.0 to 0.75. Even at z_target=4.8 (line 85), arm 3 reduces largest_component_mean from 1.0 to 0.866.
findings.implication: The hub_minus_uniform contrast cannot isolate degree-variance effects because maximizing sum(k_i^2) on a 6-neighbor lattice simultaneously packs edges into dense triangle clumps and disconnects 13% to 36% of vertices from the load-bearing spanning cluster.
findings.recommended_check: Add a connectivity and periodic-wrapping constraint to the edge-replacement proposal and introduce a joint degree-variance/triangle-penalty objective to separate hub heterogeneity from triangle condensation and fragmentation.

findings.title: Rigidity eligibility gate excludes all z <= 2.4 cases, removes kappa=0 baselines at z=3.2, and induces differential attrition
findings.evidence: Only 584 of 1,344 production cases pass the G0 > 1e-6 eligibility gate (analysis/SUMMARY.json line 12). All contrasts at z <= 2.4 have eligible_pairs = 0 (including half of selected_contrasts in analysis/SUMMARY.json lines 1451-1504). At z=3.2, central-force controls (kappa=0) have eligible_pairs = 0 (line 110), while hub_minus_uniform loses pairs at L=12 (3/4 eligible, lines 28, 30) and L=18 (2/4 eligible, lines 70, 72).
findings.implication: Complete-case conditioning prevents comparing bending-stabilized networks (kappa > 0) against central-force baselines (kappa = 0) at z=3.2 and introduces survivorship bias in hub_minus_uniform at L=12 and L=18 where more fragmented hub realizations are selectively dropped.
findings.recommended_check: Report unconditioned G0 contrasts alongside complete-case contrasts at z=2.4 and z=3.2, and evaluate sensitivity of pair retention and retention_delta_mean to varying the G0 > 1e-6 threshold between 1e-8 and 1e-4.

findings.title: Correlated PRNG streams across coordination targets z, duplicate masks, and redundant matched_final_stress metric
findings.evidence: Line 108 seeds graph() with (74000 if L==24 else 73000)+seed regardless of z, so all seven z targets in a size-seed block share the same initial edge-selection PRNG prefix (lines 12, 17); only 311 of 336 graph variants yield unique masks (analysis/SUMMARY.json line 9). In lines 95 and 100, linearity at t=0 forces s0 = 0.1*G0, making matched_final_stress (s/G0) identically 0.1 * retention (s/s0).
findings.implication: The 1,344 mechanical cases derive from only 12 size-seed blocks (4 seeds per L) with correlated trajectories across z, and matched_final_stress_delta_mean in analysis/paired-summary.csv is an exact 0.1x rescaling of retention_delta_mean rather than an independent observable.
findings.recommended_check: Spawn independent RNG streams keyed on (L, z, seed) via SeedSequence, increase seed replication per (L, z) block to power small topological contrasts, and document that matched_final_stress is algebraically 0.1 * retention in this linear model.

R2_clustering.strongest_surviving_claim: In the small-strain linearized periodic triangular lattice model with exponential internal strain-memory relaxation, the numerical implementation satisfies exact degree-sequence and directional-edge invariants for alternating-hexagon flips, passes finite-difference gradient and translational-null checks, and shows that fixed-node hub-biased edge concentration (which jointly increases degree variance, triangle clumping, and network fragmentation) consistently reduces stress retention relative to uniform networks for z >= 3.2 at kappa in {0.003, 0.03}, whereas small realized degree-preserving triangle perturbations (0.4% to 2.3% clustering shift) produce near-zero retention changes.
R2_clustering.decisive_next_experiment: Log active collinear bending motif counts (bends = nb) in the graph summary and execute a targeted sweep at L=24, z in {3.2, 4.0, 4.8} using (1) rejection-free sampling of indexed alternating hexagons with a joint Metropolis penalty on |delta_bends| to test whether larger degree-preserving clustering contrasts (delta clustering >= 0.05) can be achieved at fixed bending motif count, and (2) connectivity-preserving hub swaps that forbid disconnecting the wrapping component or altering triangle counts.

literature_to_verify.reason: Contextualize the complete exclusion of central-force (kappa=0) networks at z <= 3.2 and bending-stabilized networks at z <= 2.4 under the G0 > 1e-6 threshold.

literature_to_verify.reason: Verify known topological mobility bounds and ergodicity constraints of local alternating 6-ring flips on fixed-degree planar/toroidal lattice subgraphs.

R3_hubs.summary: Audit of the fixed-node hub-bias (arm 3) and hexagon-flip triangle interventions (arms 1–2) shows that maximizing sum(k_i^2) on a nearest-neighbor triangular lattice with hard degree ceiling k_max = 6 does not produce high-degree hubs; instead, it drives lattice-gas condensation into fully packed k ≈ 6 crystalline patches (transitivity ≈ 0.38–0.40) and k = 0 vacancies. Consequently, arm 3 co-inflates triangle counts by +48% to +209% even in the rigid regime (z >= 3.2) while depleting the giant component by 13%–36% and severing periodic percolation in a subset of z = 3.2 realizations. Conditioning mechanical contrasts on G0 > 1e-6 therefore introduces survivorship bias at z = 3.2, while degree-preserving hexagon flips (arms 1–2) perturb triangle counts by 25–60x less than arm 3, preventing an unconfounded attribution of mechanical differences to degree variance versus clustering.

findings.title: Fixed-node degree-squared bias on a k_max = 6 lattice drives edge condensation and triangle explosion rather than hub formation
findings.evidence: Arm 3 accepts direction-matched edge swaps via exp(0.6*(new-old)) on sum(k_i^2) where node degree k_i <= 6. Across L=24, z=1.2..4.8 (analysis/graph-summary.csv lines 61–85), transitivity_mean in arm 3 locks to 0.383–0.396 (near the k=6 bulk lattice limit of 6/15 = 0.40) and triangles_mean jumps by +208.5% at z=3.2 (544.5 vs 176.5) and +47.6% at z=4.8 (872.75 vs 591.25).
findings.implication: Because degrees on a nearest-neighbor triangular lattice cannot exceed 6, maximizing degree variance phase-separates edges into dense k=6 triangular clusters and k=0 voids. Mechanical contrasts for hub_minus_uniform are heavily confounded by massive triangle condensation and cannot be interpreted as the isolated effect of degree heterogeneity or scale-free-like hubs.
findings.recommended_check: Report the full node-degree distribution P(k) for k in {0..6} and implement a joint Metropolis objective that penalizes triangle changes during degree-variance swaps.

findings.title: Hub-bias fragmentation causes non-random rigidity dropouts at z = 3.2, biasing complete-case mechanical contrasts
findings.evidence: At z=3.2 (kappa=0.003 and 0.03), triangle_high_minus_low retains 4/4 eligible_pairs across all sizes, whereas hub_minus_uniform drops to 3/4 eligible_pairs at L=12 (lines 28, 30) and 2/4 at L=18 (lines 70, 72), matching the loss of periodic wrapping in arm 3 (wrap_basis_2_mean = 0.75 at L=12, analysis/graph-summary.csv line 21; 0.50 at L=18, line 49).
findings.implication: Excluding pairs that fail G0 > 1e-6 selectively removes the seeds where arm 3 fragmentation severs the load-bearing percolating backbone (G0 ~ 0), biasing G0_delta_mean upward (+0.0509 at L=18, z=3.2) through survivorship bias.
findings.recommended_check: Report unconditioned G0_delta_mean (retaining G0 = 0 nonrigid states) alongside the G0 > 1e-6 gated values, and stratify contrasts by periodic wrapping status.

findings.title: Giant-component node depletion in arm 3 inflates effective subgraph coordination while stress remains normalized by total N
findings.evidence: At L=24, arm 3 reduces largest_component_mean from 0.985–1.000 (arms 0–2) to 0.638 at z=3.2 (line 77), 0.755 at z=4.0 (line 81), and 0.866 at z=4.8 (line 85), with susceptibility_mean ~ 1.00–1.11 indicating isolated k=0 nodes, while source/cpu-sweep.py line 93 normalizes stress by full lattice area N*sqrt(3)/2.
findings.implication: Concentrating all M = z*N/2 edges onto 64%–87% of the nodes raises the effective coordination within the active giant component to z_eff ~ z / largest_component_mean in [5.0, 5.5], shifting arm 3 from a bending-dominated network into a locally overconstrained, stretching-dominated patch where axial relaxation (r=0.5) strongly reduces stress retention.
findings.recommended_check: Compute effective coordination z_eff, triangle density, and modulus normalized by the active giant-component node count N_LC to test how much of retention_delta_mean is explained by subgraph densification.

findings.title: Degree-preserving hexagon flips produce 25–60x smaller triangle perturbations than hub bias, confounding effect-size comparisons
findings.evidence: Because arms 1–2 require alternating 6-rings (source/cpu-sweep.py line 33) and preserve exact node degrees, accepted moves at L=24, z=4.8 average 114.75 and 112.0 out of 57600 proposals (~0.2%), shifting triangles_mean by only 4.5 (593.5 vs 589.0, 0.76% of baseline) compared to +281.5 (+47.6%) in arm 3 (line 85); at L=24, z=3.2 the shift is 11.0 vs +368.0 triangles (lines 74–77).
findings.implication: Near-zero retention and modulus differences in triangle_high_minus_low (analysis/paired-summary.csv lines 113–127) reflect the narrow topological reach of alternating-hexagon flips at fixed degree sequence rather than evidence that clustering is mechanically negligible compared with degree variance.
findings.recommended_check: Report mechanical contrasts normalized per unit change in transitivity or triangle count, or introduce a rewiring arm that varies clustering without strict alternating-hexagon constraints.

findings.title: Periodic wrapping booleans and whole-grid clustering_mean exhibit metric artifacts under oblique steps and node isolation
findings.evidence: In line 60, wrap[k] |= diff[k] != 0 accumulates across all components and sets both wrap[0] and wrap[1] to True for a single 1D cycle along steps[2] = (-1, 1) where diff = [-L, L]. In line 63, local assigns 0 to nodes with degree <= 1 and averages over all N nodes, so arm 3's k=0 vacancies dilute clustering_mean relative to transitivity_mean.
findings.implication: wrap_basis_1 and wrap_basis_2 can both read True for a 1D diagonal filament (rank-1 winding) or across separate components without 2D spanning percolation, and whole-grid clustering_mean understates local clustering inside the active subgraph of arm 3.
findings.recommended_check: Compute the rank of the winding-vector matrix per connected component to distinguish 1D vs 2D periodic percolation, and report mean local clustering conditioned on nodes with k_i >= 2.

R3_hubs.strongest_surviving_claim: Within the small-strain linearized triangular-lattice model with selective axial relaxation (r = 0.5) and collinear bending (kappa in {0.003, 0.03}), direction-matched edge condensation via the sum(k_i^2) MCMC intervention (arm 3) at high nominal coordination (z = 4.0 and 4.8, where all 4 seed pairs per size are rigid and percolating) reproducibly lowers stress retention and G0-matched final stress relative to uniform bond dilution (arm 0), whereas degree-preserving alternating-hexagon flips (arm 1 vs arm 2) produce only minor topological and mechanical shifts.
R3_hubs.decisive_next_experiment: Run a two-parameter constrained-MCMC sweep on the L=24 lattice at z in {3.2, 4.0, 4.8} using joint energy E = -beta_k * sum(k_i^2) - beta_T * T while rejecting moves that create degree-0 nodes or disconnect the giant component; this will separate (1) degree variance at fixed giant-component size and matched triangle count from (2) lattice-gas void formation and triangle condensation.
